### Sample ID options

Options for adding the id to .obs on the MuData object. Having a sample
id present in a requirement of several components for this pipeline.

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--add_id_to_obs`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Add the value passed with --id to .obs.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean`

[Default]{.arg-key} `true`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--add_id_obs_output`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
.Obs column to add the sample IDs to. Required and only used when
--add_id_to_obs is set to 'true'
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"sample_id"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--add_id_make_observation_keys_unique`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Join the id to the .obs index (.obs_names).
Only used when --add_id_to_obs is set to 'true'.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean`

[Default]{.arg-key} `true`
:::
::::
:::::

### Mitochondrial & Ribosomal Gene Detection

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--var_gene_names`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
.var column name to be used to detect mitochondrial/ribosomal genes instead of .var_names (default if not set).
Gene names matching with the regex value from --mitochondrial_gene_regex or --ribosomal_gene_regex will be
identified as mitochondrial or ribosomal genes, respectively.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"gene_symbol"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--var_name_mitochondrial_genes`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
In which .var slot to store a boolean array corresponding the mitochondrial genes.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_name_mitochondrial_fraction`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
When specified, write the fraction of counts originating from mitochondrial genes
(based on --mitochondrial_gene_regex) to an .obs column with the specified name.
Requires --var_name_mitochondrial_genes.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--mitochondrial_gene_regex`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Regex string that identifies mitochondrial genes from --var_gene_names.
By default will detect human and mouse mitochondrial genes from a gene symbol.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"^[mM][tT]-"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--var_name_ribosomal_genes`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
In which .var slot to store a boolean array corresponding the ribosomal genes.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_name_ribosomal_fraction`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
When specified, write the fraction of counts originating from ribosomal genes
(based on --ribosomal_gene_regex) to an .obs column with the specified name.
Requires --var_name_ribosomal_genes.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--ribosomal_gene_regex`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Regex string that identifies ribosomal genes from --var_gene_names.
By default will detect human and mouse ribosomal genes from a gene symbol.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"^[Mm]?[Rr][Pp][LlSs]"`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/multiomics/process_singlesample/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/workflows/multiomics/process_singlesample);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/multiomics/process_singlesample/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
